challenge: NodeKit had canonical Caseflow lifecycle records, NodeTrace trajectories, and NodeProof receipts, but no first-class compiler that turned an approved project journey into a bounded execution graph with typed artifact handoffs, safe parallelism, durable task handles, and a derived runnable frontier.
observedFailure: The architecture existed only as discussion and documentation. An orchestrator could invent node types, parallelize conflicting work, treat fresh context as evaluator independence, aggregate before all evidence arrived, or let a generated design file drift into a second authority.
resolution: Added a public graph-of-bounded-loops compiler with the fixed eleven-node vocabulary, deterministic graph, edge, task, and trace identities, declared read/write/external-system authority, disjoint fan-out validation, exact materialized edge handoffs with artifact-ref and digest arrays, bounded attempts and events, headless versus headful browser lanes, qualified independent evaluator enforcement, upstream human gates for external writes, replay-based NodeProof, generated non-authoritative design Markdown, and a fail-closed sequential-versus-graph brownfield experiment evaluator enforcing the zero-conflict, fully hashed, no-drop, no-false-advance, no-missed-critical, proof-valid, and 20%-time-or-30%-defect gates. Caseflow remains canonical and automatic promotion remains disabled.
knownLimitations: A real coding-agent sequential-versus-graph campaign on the same frozen brownfield task remains a separate evidence run.
Consumer-specific model qualification receipts and signed-in Chrome proofs remain consumer evidence.
Canonical promotion requires a separately verified named-human approval.
